* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

Human Bap31 and all orthologs to yeast

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**

Erroneous annotation

This seems odd. Bap31 appears to act upstream of the ER exit site, which implies it is acting as a chaperone in the ER with downstream effects on transport (it might even be associated with the translocon, which would make it quite indirect). This fits interpretation with the other existing  annotation on the human Bap31

Claude review

This is a really sharp critique, and you're touching on a genuine interpretive tension in the literature. Let me lay out the specific problems with the "cargo receptor" conclusion:
What the data actually show:

Binding starts too early. The interaction begins at the time of heavy chain association with β2-microglobulin and is maintained until the class I molecule has left [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15187134/) the ER. That's the very beginning of MHC I assembly — far upstream of any ER exit site decision. A classic cargo receptor would be expected to engage cargo at or near ER exit sites, not at the earliest folding steps.
It's embedded in the peptide-loading complex. Bap31 is part of the peptide-loading complex and can bind to tapasin in the absence of class I. [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15187134/) This places Bap31's primary function squarely in ER quality control and peptide loading — upstream activity — which makes the export delay on knockdown potentially just an indirect consequence of disrupted upstream processing.
Knockout only delays, not abolishes export. Cells lacking the two Bap proteins maintain surface levels of class I comparable to those of controls. [PubMed Central](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1978250/) A genuine cargo receptor would be expected to be more essential to export. A mere delay is more consistent with a chaperone/quality control role where other pathways compensate.
The KKXX motif points the other way. Bap31 has a dilysine motif at its C-terminus, which is known to act as a retrieval signal from post-ER compartments via COPI-coated vesicles. [Molecular Biology of the Cell](https://www.molbiolcell.org/doi/10.1091/mbc.e07-08-0781) That's a retention/retrieval signal, not an export one — which fits better with a quality control chaperone that cycles within the ER than with a dedicated anterograde cargo receptor.

Where the cargo receptor model gets its best support:
The strongest evidence comes from a 2001 paper establishing that ER-to-Golgi transport of MHC class I molecules is independent of their cytoplasmic tails, which lack ER export motifs — consistent with receptor-mediated exit — and that MHC class I molecules accumulate at ER exit sites from which TAP molecules are excluded. [ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1074761300000819) Since MHC I has no intrinsic export signal, something must act as a receptor. Bap31 is a plausible candidate, but identifying it as the receptor requires more than correlation.
The bottom line:
You're right to be skeptical. The experiments are largely consistent with Bap31 being a quality control chaperone that escorts MHC I through folding and peptide loading in the ER, and the colocalization with mSec31/COPII markers could simply reflect the fact that properly-assembled cargo (which Bap31 helped produce) ends up at exit sites — not that Bap31 is actively recruiting it there. The "cargo receptor" label is an interpretation that outstrips what the knockdown and co-precipitation data can definitively support. The authors acknowledge as much by consistently calling it a putative cargo receptor rather than a proven one.Want to be notified when Claude responds?NotifySonnet 4.6Adaptive

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Very interesting update. Despite the large number of primary annotations (CC and BP), we never had the right term. For example, we had endoplasmic reticulum, membrane, and a bunch of other membranes, but never “endoplasmic reticulum membrane.” Also, for MF, I would suggest the term GO:0140388 protein translocation chaperone activity but it is not yet available for PAINT, as it is too recent. I will close the ticket once I have finished annotating the family.
Thanks a lot,
Marc.
